tools.description:
Get this MCP server's own version, active capability profile,
        registered tool counts, and WRITE/Tier-1/ADR-017 state — so a
        client can determine actual capability and safety state without
        inference. Read-only, local only: makes no pfSense API call.

        Every field is a deterministic local fact, independently and
        redundantly enforced elsewhere (capability gating, the empty
        WriteEndpoints allow-list, CI-enforced Tier 1/ADR-017 isolation
        tests) — this tool only reports already-enforced state and
        cannot itself grant or change any capability.
tools.name: pfsense_mcp_info

active_capability_set.description: Capability names granted to this server instance's active profile (the same set ToolRegistry used to decide what to register).
active_capability_set.title: Active Capability Set

active_profile.description: This server instance's active capability profile name.
active_profile.title: Active Profile

active_write_capabilities.description: Of active_capability_set, the entries whose name ends in _WRITE. Always empty in this build — independently, redundantly re-verified by scripts/write_capability_check.py in CI.
active_write_capabilities.title: Active Write Capabilities

active_write_endpoint_count.description: Entries in the WriteEndpoints mutation allow-list. Always 0 in this build. This is the allow-list WriteApiClient.execute() itself consults before any network call — not a separate, potentially-drifting count.
active_write_endpoint_count.title: Active Write Endpoint Count

guidance_imported_this_process.description: Whether pfsense_mcp.guidance has been imported anywhere in this running process (sys.modules check). Expected to always be false — no READ tool or Tier 1 path consumes it yet. Same caveat as tier1_imported_this_process: observed runtime evidence, not a substitute for CI-enforced isolation.
guidance_imported_this_process.title: Guidance Imported This Process

guidance_package_present.description: Whether pfsense_mcp.guidance (ADR-017's official documentation guidance layer) is present in this installed distribution — packaging fact only.
guidance_package_present.title: Guidance Package Present

mcp_transport.description: The MCP transport this build serves over. Always 'stdio'.
mcp_transport.title: Mcp Transport

registered_read_tool_count.description: Of registered_tool_count, how many are READ tools.
registered_read_tool_count.title: Registered Read Tool Count

registered_tool_count.description: Total MCP tools actually registered on this running instance (after capability and PFSENSE_ALLOWED_TOOLS filtering) — includes this tool itself.
registered_tool_count.title: Registered Tool Count

registered_write_tool_count.description: Of registered_tool_count, how many are WRITE tools. Always 0 in this build — register_all_write() registers nothing.
registered_write_tool_count.title: Registered Write Tool Count

tier1_imported_this_process.description: Whether pfsense_mcp.tier1 has been imported anywhere in this running process (sys.modules check). Expected to always be false. This is observed runtime evidence, not a substitute for the structural isolation CI enforces (tests/tier1/test_isolation.py) — a false value here does not itself prove unreachability, only that nothing has imported it yet in this process.
tier1_imported_this_process.title: Tier1 Imported This Process

tier1_package_present.description: Whether pfsense_mcp.tier1 is present in this installed distribution (a packaging fact, not a capability — Tier 1 registers no tool and is never imported by production bootstrap, independent of whether it is present).
tier1_package_present.title: Tier1 Package Present
